# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 103 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 103 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_103_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 20

**1** "Lord," I said, "I want to ask about one more thing." "What is it?" he said. "What are the stones taken from the deep and fitted into the tower — and who are the twenty men who carried them?" **2** "The stones from the deep," he said, "are the first — those who believed before the Son of God was revealed in the world. They went down into the water dead and came up alive, knowing the name of the Son of God. That is why they were brought up from the deep — so they could be fitted into the building of the tower. **3** They were sealed before they went down. The twenty men who carried them — these are the apostles and teachers of the proclamation of the Son of God." **4** "But why did the virgins also carry the stones?" I asked. **5** "Because the virgins had to come first and carry the stones into the building. Without the power of the virgins, these stones could never have been placed into the tower — there would have been no fulness of life." **6** Then he showed me again the great banquet of the Son of God, with all the elect gathered at the table. **7** And the tall man — the Son of God — moved about among them rejoicing greatly, and the whole tower was filled with the joy of the Lord. **8** And the twelve virgins danced around the tower. And when I asked what the great banquet was, he said, "This is the joy of the Lord at the completion of the tower."

---

*EMET: the pre-Christian faithful who believed before the revelation of the Son went down "dead" and came up "alive" — a retroactive application of baptismal theology to the righteous of the Old Testament. The joy of the completed tower is the eschatological banquet.*
